content:
幾個月前，MacBook Neo 震撼登場，成為 2026 年最具性價比的手提電腦。即使最近加價後，它仍然是大多數人最推薦的入門級手提電腦。正如 Apple 其他高性價比的產品一樣，他們也加入了一些玩味十足的顏色，例如柑橘色、珊瑚色、靛藍色和銀色，為這些 MacBook 增添個性與色彩。不過，我最不滿的是，大部分 MacBook 配件的顏色都只配襯傳統的銀色或太空灰。這時 Satechi 就推出了一系列顏色匹配的配件

I actually reviewed the "big brother" version of this product before and really liked it. It's the most versatile accessory in Satechi's new lineup. It can expand one of your USB-C ports into 5 additional ports, and it's reasonably sized. About the size of a hockey puck, and it has built-in MagSafe. So you can use it with both your MacBook Neo and iPhone. This USB-C hub provides:

  • HDMI output supporting up to 4K video at 60Hz
  • USB-C pass-through charging up to 60W
  • USB-C port with transfer speeds up to 5Gbps
  • USB-A port with transfer speeds up to 5Gbps
  • Standard SD card reader
  • An elegant nylon braided USB-C cable

Since it has MagSafe, they include an adhesive magnetic ring that you can stick to the lid of your MacBook Neo. On top of that, they color-matched the metal ring to the Neo! So when you're not using the hub, the magnetic ring doesn't look out of place. As I mentioned, this is my personal favorite product because of how versatile it is. It's compact, well-made, has most of the major ports people need, and works with a variety of devices.

The OntheGo multiport adapter is available in the same colors as the MacBook Neo, now on sale at Amazon and Satechi's website for $44.99.

This one has the more traditional USB-C hub form factor that you're familiar with. It snaps directly onto the side of the MacBook Neo (hence the "Snap hub" name) and adds six new ports, one more than the OntheGo hub mentioned above. You can tell at a glance that it was designed for the MacBook Neo because it fits so securely once attached. The Snap Hub provides:

  • SD and MicroSD card readers
  • USB-C pass-through charging up to 45W (enough to charge the MacBook Neo, since the Neo only supports up to 30W)

The Snap Hub is definitely the most seamlessly integrated of the three accessories — it feels like a product Apple would have made itself. It features a two-tone design where the top matches the Neo's material and color perfectly, but they cleverly made the rest of the housing a soft-touch rubber because they know the hub will be sitting against the Neo's metal chassis, and metal on metal usually isn't a great combination. I think that's an excellent design choice. One thing to note is that this hub takes up two of the Neo's USB-C ports, but the hub itself still provides two USB-C ports and an additional one

The USB-C snap-on hub is available starting today in the four Neo colors we mentioned, priced the same as the OntheGo Hub at $44.99, on Amazon and Satechi's website.

To round out Satechi's new Neo lineup, they redesigned the Slim EX mouse in matching colors. I previously tested the non-color version of this mouse, and thanks to its value, it's one of the easiest products to recommend. For just $29, you get:

  • Connect up to 3 different devices simultaneously — two via Bluetooth and one via a 2.4GHz receiver (and it's a USB-C receiver!)
  • Aluminum body
  • Charges via USB-C
  • User-replaceable battery
  • Three months of continuous use, over a year of battery life in sleep mode
  • Also includes a USB-C cable for charging and connection

The build quality and feel of this mouse rival mice that cost twice as much. It has a sleek, low-profile aluminum body that's comfortable even during extended use. Switching between devices is quick and very practical for me, as I frequently switch between my MacBook and iPad. And the fact that the 2.4GHz receiver is USB-C instead of USB-A is a genuinely underrated upgrade. Although the Neo's trackpad is already excellent, I personally like using both a trackpad and a mouse together. I use the trackpad for gestures and horizontal scrolling, while I use the mouse for more precise

The Slim EX wireless mouse is available in the four colors we mentioned, as well as the previously available black. The mouse is priced at $29.99 and is available on Amazon and Satechi's website. If you want to save a bit, the black version of the mouse is identical and is currently on sale for $23.99.

Conclusion

Satechi is the first brand to launch these color-matched accessories for the MacBook Neo, and they clearly understand their target audience. They've brought high-quality, functional accessories to the MacBook Neo lineup — accessories that fill the gaps left by the compromises Neo made to keep its price at $699. All of these accessories are well-made, offer plenty of practical features, and enhance the MacBook Neo experience.

If I had to pick one from this bunch, I'd lean slightly toward the OntheGo multiport adapter, purely because of its versatility and the fact that any device with a USB-C port and MagSafe can use it. But the Snap Hub is also great — its physical integration with the Neo is excellent — and the Slim EX mouse is a nice bonus. What do you think? Are these accessories worth buying? How important is color matching to you? Let's discuss in the comments!
